title: Multi-Agent RL Under Degraded Communications
summary: A from-scratch two-robot gridworld (extending my Senior Design project) that measures how losing the radio link hurts cooperating robots and compares the old 'Hold when degraded' rule with tabular Q-learning, DQN, and a DQN with memory of the ally's last-known position on held-out maps.
headline: With the link down 90% of the time, the original Hold rule completed 17.6% of missions (7.8% in close quarters) while a DQN with last-known-ally memory completed 98.6% (96.0%), mean of 5 seeds on held-out layouts.
